full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J.—This Revisions application under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is directed against the order date 20.4.81 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, First Court, Chittagong in Criminal Motion No. 199 of 1979 and against the order dated 19.3.79 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Cox's Bazar Chittagong in Misc. Case No. 43 of 1976-77. 

 2. Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that some disputed lands were attached under the accused provision of section 145(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. For granting yearly lease for manufacturing salt the Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Cox's Bazar, Chittagong held an open bid auction of the proceeding lands for the Bengali year 1385.86 on 5.3.79. The petitioner Abdul Hamid being the highest bidder auction purchased the proceeding lands for Tk. 28,050/- for the Bengali year 1385-86 and paid Tk. 6,380/- as part payment of the bid money on 5.3.79. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate fixed 9.3.79. for payment of the balance auction money, failing which, it was ordered, the deposited money would be forfeited to the Government. On 9.3.79 the petitioner paid Tk. 3,620/-only. Upon his prayer the petitioner was allowed 7 days time to pay up the balance auction money. The petitioner was ordered to deposit the balance auction money on 17.3.79 failing which, it was further ordered, all the deposited auction money would be forfeited. On 17.3.79 the S Magistrate was otherwise busy and the case came up for hearing on 19.3.79. The petitioner prayed for one month's time to deposit the balance auction money. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate rejected the prayer for time and forfeited the entire deposited money amounting to Tk. 10,000/- to the State. He passed order for issue of notice fixing 25.3.79 for holding fresh auction. 

 7. A court or public servant or any person who holds auction of any property has the power and jurisdiction to lay down the conditions of auction. A court of law may only see that the condition or conditions are not unconscionable, illegal or unreasonable. The learned Magistrate in the present case has not imposed any unconscionable, illegal or unreasonable condition.
